Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and the required wake-visual skill, then inspect the current rollout evidence and inherited guidance/logs before touching the policy. I’ll keep the work confined to this Phase 2 workspace and won’t consult any omitted or neighboring research shelf.

The wake-visual skill applies here: it requires comparing the best finite rollout with the most informative failure sheet, anchoring image observations to metrics/diagnostics, and writing the visual diagnosis before the candidate edit. I’m following that ordering now.

The evidence inventory has no semantic failure rollout: every available sampled and inherited evaluation reaches the target. I’ll therefore use the assigned guidance’s documented target-blind boundary-exit as the failure boundary, and visually compare the best successful controller with the most degraded successful inherited perturbation instead of inventing a failure case.

The strongest evidence is now clear: gain `1.7` is the measured anchor, while `1.72`, `1.725`, and `1.9` all retain capture but regress in arrival, mean distance, crossflow, and loads. The keyframes show the same self-propelled turn-and-diagonal topology, so I’m treating this as a narrow steering sensitivity—not evidence for adding wake signals or changing propulsion—and will document a single lower-side bracket test before editing.

The candidate and durable guidance are now updated together: one parameter-only lower-side bracket (`steering_gain=1.68`) and one materially revised lesson that incorporates the parent failure boundary, sampled `1.7/1.9` results, and inherited `1.72/1.725` regressions. I’m moving to the mandated repository checks; no CFD will be run.
